intro.title: Compound Component (Tabs)
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a tabbed interface using Vue's compound component pattern. You'll create a set of components—Tabs, TabList, and TabPanel—that work together to manage and display content in separate tabs. The core concept is using Vue's provide/inject API to share state and methods between parent and child components without prop drilling. You'll learn to structure components for reusability and maintain a clean separation of concerns. By the end, you'll have a functional tab system where clicking a tab button shows its corresponding content panel.
intro.usecase: Compound components like Tabs are essential in modern web applications where complex UI needs to be modular and reusable. You'll find them in dashboard interfaces where users switch between different data views, in e-commerce product pages that toggle between descriptions, reviews, and specifications, and in settings panels that organize options into categorized sections. As a Vue developer, you'll implement this pattern to create maintainable tabbed navigation for admin panels, user profiles, or multi-step forms where content needs logical grouping without tight coupling between components.

objectives: Construct a Vue component that manages the active tab state using the Composition API
Implement child components that receive and respond to parent-provided context
Configure slot-based content distribution for dynamic tab panels
Bind click handlers to tab headers to control panel visibility
Integrate provide/inject patterns to share state between compound components
Manipulate CSS classes conditionally to visually indicate the active tab
Render a complete tab interface with interactive headers and corresponding content panels

steps.title: Import Vue and ref
steps.instruction: Import Vue and the ref function from the 'vue' package.
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in Vue and ref from 'vue'.
steps.analogousExample:
// Importing from a package
import { createApp, ref } from 'vue'
steps.expectedOutcome: The Vue framework and ref function are imported and available for use.
successCriteria: Vue and ref are imported from 'vue'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're importing both Vue and ref from the 'vue' package.
steps.feedbackWrong: That's not quite right. You need to import both Vue and ref from 'vue' to proceed.

steps.title: Create Tabs component
steps.instruction: Create a Vue component named Tabs with a template section that returns a div wrapper.
steps.hint: Define a component that exports an object with a template property containing a div element.
steps.seedCode:
// Import Vue and ref from 'vue'

// Create Tabs component here
steps.expectedOutcome: A Tabs component with a template that renders a div element.
successCriteria: Tabs component is defined with a template property containing a div element.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created the Tabs component structure.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've defined a component named Tabs with a template property.
steps.feedbackWrong: The Tabs component isn't properly defined. Check that you've created a component with a template.

steps.title: Initialize active tab state
steps.instruction: Inside your Tabs component, initialize a reactive state variable named activeTab using ref, with a default value of 0.
steps.hint: Use const activeTab = ref(0) to create a reactive reference that tracks which tab is currently active.
steps.analogousExample:
// Similar: reactive state for a counter
const count = ref(0);
steps.expectedOutcome: The Tabs component now has a reactive activeTab state that will track the currently selected tab.
successCriteria: activeTab is declared using ref with an initial value of 0 inside the setup function.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using ref(0) to initialize the state with a default value of 0.
steps.feedbackWrong: The activeTab state wasn't properly initialized. Remember to use ref(0) inside the setup function.

steps.title: Create TabList component
steps.instruction: Create a TabList component that accepts children via slots. Define it as a Vue component object with a setup function that returns a render function.
steps.hint: Create a new component constant named TabList. In its setup function, return a render function that renders the children passed via slots.
steps.expectedOutcome: A TabList component is defined that can accept and render children via slots.
successCriteria: TabList component is created as a Vue component object with a setup function that returns a render function using slots.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've created a TabList component, but make sure it properly accepts and renders children via slots in its render function.
steps.feedbackWrong: The TabList component is not correctly defined. It should be a Vue component object with a setup function that returns a render function using slots.

steps.title: Create Tab component
steps.instruction: Create a Tab component that accepts index and label props. The component should return a button element with the label text.
steps.hint: Define a Vue component that takes props and returns a button with the label prop as its content.
steps.expectedOutcome: A Tab component is defined with props and returns a button element.
successCriteria: Tab component is created with props for index and label, and returns a button element containing the label.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've created a component, but make sure it accepts both index and label props and returns a button with the label.
steps.feedbackWrong: The Tab component is missing or incorrect. It should accept index and label props and return a button with the label.

steps.title: Create TabPanels component
steps.instruction: Create a TabPanels component that accepts children via slots. The component should be a simple container that renders its slot content.
steps.hint: Define a new component object with a setup function that returns the slot content.
steps.expectedOutcome: You should have a TabPanels component that can render slot content.
successCriteria: TabPanels component is created with a setup function that returns slot content.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created the TabPanels container component.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure TabPanels has a setup function that returns the slot content.
steps.feedbackWrong: TabPanels component is missing or incomplete. Create a component with a setup function that returns slot content.

steps.title: Create TabPanel component
steps.instruction: Create a TabPanel component that accepts index and content props. Define it as a functional component that returns the content prop.
steps.hint: The TabPanel component should be a simple component that receives props and renders the content. Use props.index and props.content to access the passed values.
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have a TabPanel component that can receive index and content props and render the content.
successCriteria: TabPanel component is defined as a functional component that accepts props and returns props.content.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've started creating TabPanel, but make sure it accepts props and returns props.content. Check that you're using the correct prop names.
steps.feedbackWrong: The TabPanel component is not defined correctly. It should be a functional component that takes props and returns the content prop.

steps.title: Define tab click handler
steps.instruction: Inside the Tabs component's setup function, define a selectTab function that takes an index parameter and updates the activeTab ref to that index.
steps.hint: Create a function that sets the activeTab.value to the provided index parameter.
steps.expectedOutcome: A selectTab function is defined inside the Tabs component that can update the active tab state.
successCriteria: The selectTab function is defined with an index parameter and updates activeTab.value to that index.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your function takes an index parameter and sets activeTab.value to that index.
steps.feedbackWrong: The selectTab function should be defined inside the Tabs component's setup function and update the activeTab state.

steps.title: Add TabList to Tabs template
steps.instruction: In the Tabs component's setup return object, add a render function that returns a div containing a TabList component with a default slot.
steps.hint: The render function should return a div element with TabList as its child. Use the default slot to allow TabList to render its children.
steps.expectedOutcome: The Tabs component now has a render function that returns a div containing a TabList component with a default slot.
successCriteria: The Tabs component's setup returns a render function that renders a div with TabList and a default slot.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure the render function returns a div containing TabList with a default slot.
steps.feedbackWrong: The Tabs component should have a render function returning a div with TabList and a default slot. Check the structure.

steps.title: Wire Tab components with click handler
steps.instruction: In the Tab component, add props to receive the tab index, activeTab state, and selectTab handler.
steps.hint: Add a props object in the Tab component to define the expected properties.
steps.expectedOutcome: The Tab component will be ready to receive the necessary data and functions from its parent.
successCriteria: Tab component has a props array containing 'index', 'activeTab', and 'selectTab'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some props, but make sure to include all three: index, activeTab, and selectTab.
steps.feedbackWrong: The Tab component needs props defined. Add a props array with 'index', 'activeTab', and 'selectTab'.

steps.title: Add TabPanels to Tabs template
steps.instruction: In the Tabs component's template, add the TabPanels component as a child element after the TabList.
steps.hint: Place the TabPanels component inside the template, similar to how you added TabList.
steps.expectedOutcome: The Tabs template now contains both TabList and TabPanels components.
successCriteria: TabPanels component is added to the Tabs template after TabList.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've added TabPanels to the Tabs template, not just created the component.
steps.feedbackWrong: The TabPanels component needs to be added to the Tabs template. Look at how TabList was added and follow the same pattern.

steps.title: Wire TabPanel components with active state
steps.instruction: In the TabPanel component, add a prop called 'index' and use v-show to conditionally display the panel only when its index matches the activeTab value from the Tabs component.
steps.hint: Add props: ['index'] to the TabPanel component, then use v-show="index === activeTab" on the root div element in the template.
steps.expectedOutcome: Each TabPanel will only be visible when its index matches the currently active tab, creating the tab switching behavior.
successCriteria: TabPanel component has props: ['index'] and uses v-show="index === activeTab" in its template.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but check that you've added both the 'index' prop and the v-show directive with the correct condition.
steps.feedbackWrong: The TabPanel component needs both the index prop and conditional display logic. Try adding props: ['index'] and v-show="index === activeTab" to the template.
